name: Basketball
weather_note: Early June peak pre-monsoon heat in Marredpally. Low rain chance (~10%). Humidity around 45%. Schedule matches early morning and stay hydrated.
rules_text:
1. Team Composition
Each team shall consist of 5 players on court.
A minimum of 1 female player must be present on the court at all times.
Each team may register up to 3 substitute players, including at least 1 female substitute.


2. Match Format
Each match shall be played for 10 minutes.( 5 minute halves with 5 minute break time at half time )
The team with the higher score at the end of regulation time shall be declared the winner.
Standard basketball rules shall apply unless otherwise specified by the tournament organizers.



3. Tournament Format
The tournament shall follow a Round Robin Format.
Teams shall be assigned as Team A, Team B, and Team C through a draw of QR codes.
Matches shall be conducted in the following order:
Team A vs Team B
Team B vs Team C
Team C vs Team A
The team losing Match 1 shall play Match 2 against Team C.
If the losing team from Match 1 also loses Match 2, the Final shall be conducted between the remaining two teams.
If each team records one win and one loss, the total points scored across all league matches shall be considered and the top two teams shall qualify for the Final.
If two teams remain tied on total points scored, a 5-point Tie-Breaker Match shall be conducted to determine qualification for the Final.

4. Final Match
The two qualified teams shall compete in the Final.
The team with the higher score at the end of regulation time shall be declared the Champion.

5. Tie-Breaker Rules
If the Final ends in a tie, the total points scored across all tournament matches (including league matches) shall be considered.
The team with the higher cumulative tournament score shall be declared the Winner.
If the cumulative tournament scores are also equal, a 5-point Tie-Breaker Match shall be played.
The winner of the Tie-Breaker Match shall be declared the Champion.

6. Referees & Officials
All matches shall be conducted under the supervision of appointed referees and tournament officials.
Standard basketball rules shall govern gameplay, substitutions, fouls, and scoring.
Any dispute arising during the tournament shall be resolved by the referees and tournament officials.
The decision of the referees and tournament officials shall be final and binding on all participants.

7. Awards
 Winners: 300 Team Points
 Runners-Up: 150 Team Points

name: Tug of War
weather_note: Ground may be slightly muddy — check terrain before matches.
rules_text:
1. Team Composition
Each team shall consist of 10 players on the rope.
A minimum of 3 female players must be on the rope at all times.
Each team may register up to 5 substitute players.
Substitutions may only be made between matches.
2. Match Format
Each match shall be played on a Best of 3 Sets basis.
The first team to win 2 sets shall be declared the winner of the match.
A set shall be won when a team successfully pulls the opposing team's side marker across the
designated winning line as determined by the referee.
A center mark shall be placed on the rope, along with two side markers positioned at equal
distances from the center mark.
A center line shall be marked on the ground.
The referee shall use these markings to determine the winner of each pull.
3. Tournament Format
The tournament shall follow a Round Robin Format.
Teams shall be assigned as Team A, Team B, and Team C through a draw.
Match Schedule
Team A vs Team B
Team B vs Team C
Team C vs Team A
If one team loses both league matches, the other two teams shall qualify for the Final.
If all three teams record one win each, the number of sets won shall be considered.
The two teams with the higher number of sets won shall qualify for the Final.
If teams remain tied on sets won, a single Tie-Breaker Pull shall be conducted.
The winner of the Tie-Breaker Pull shall qualify for the Final.
4. Final Match
The two qualified teams shall compete in the Final.
The Final shall be played on a Best of 3 Sets basis.
The first team to win 2 sets shall be declared the Champion.
5. Referees & Officials
All matches shall be conducted under the supervision of appointed referees and officials.
The decision of the referees and officials shall be final and binding on all participants.

6. Awards
Winners: 300 Team Points
Runners-Up: 150 Team Points
Gifts and Certificates will be distributed on the same day

name: Kabaddi
weather_note: Plan early morning slot before afternoon showers.
rules_text:
1. General Rules
• Kabaddi is a Men's Event. Only male participants are eligible to compete.
• The objective of the game is to score more points than the opposing team.
• A player enters the opponent's half as a Raider and attempts to touch one or more opponents before
returning safely to his own half.
• Each opponent touched by the raider is worth 1 point if the raider returns safely.
• If the raider is tackled and prevented from returning, the defending team earns 1 point and the raider
is declared out.
• Only hand and leg touches are permitted. Kicking below the head and pushing is allowed. Punching,
slapping, striking, or deliberately hitting another participant is prohibited and will result in a penalty of
5 points or disqualification at the referee's discretion.
• Only Back Kicks and Thrust Kicks are permitted (see reference image provided separately). Any other
form of kicking is not allowed.
• Pushing is only permitted to push a raider out of the court boundary. Pushing for any other purpose is
not allowed.
• Any controversy or dispute regarding kicking or pushing during play shall be decided solely by the
referee, and the decision shall be final.
• Abusive language, dangerous play, and unsportsmanlike conduct are prohibited.
• The traditional Kabaddi chant ('Kabaddi-Kabaddi') must be continuously chanted by the raider during
the raid, without taking a breath. Failure to chant continuously will result in the raider being declared
out.
• Participants must follow all instructions given by referees and officials.
• The decision of the referees and officials shall be final and binding on all participants.
• No shoes are allowed on the court. All players must play barefoot.
• All players must trim their finger nails and toe nails short before participating.
2. Understanding the Game
How to Score
• Each raid shall last a maximum of 30 seconds. A raider must cross back into his own half within this
time, or he will be declared out.
• Touch an opponent and return safely to your half = 1 point per player touched.
• Stop a raider from returning = 1 point for the defending team.
• Empty Raid: If a raider crosses into the opponent's half, does not attempt to touch any defender, and
returns without scoring, it is declared an Empty Raid. No points are awarded to either team, but it
counts toward the raid count.
• Super Tackle: If a defending team tackles a raider while 3 or fewer defenders remain on the court
(i.e., the defending team is down to its last few players) and successfully stops the raider, the
defending team is awarded 2 points instead of 1 for that tackle.
When a Player is Out
• He is touched by a raider who returns safely.
• He steps outside the boundary line.
• He is tackled as a raider before returning to his half.
Returning to the Court
• Every time a team scores a point, one previously out player may return to the court.
• Players return in the same order in which they went out.
• Revival Rule: A player who is declared out may be revived and sent back onto the court as per the
points scored by his team, in accordance with the standard revival process applicable for the
tournament; this is in addition to, and works together with, the standard point-based return rule above.
All-Out Rule
• If all 7 players of a team are declared out, it is an All-Out.
• The opposing team receives 2 bonus points.
• All 7 players return to the court and play continues.
Bonus Point
• When 6 or more defenders are on the court, a raider may attempt to earn 1 Bonus Point by legally
crossing the bonus line.
• A bonus point does not declare any defender out.
3. Team Composition
• Each team shall consist of 7 players on the court.
• Each team may register up to 5 substitute players.
• Substitutions may only be made between matches or with referee approval in case of injury.
• Active/Tactical Substitutions are also allowed during the course of the game, in addition to the
substitutions permitted above.
4. Tournament Format
• The tournament shall follow a Round Robin Format.
• Teams shall be assigned as Team A, Team B, and Team C through a draw.
Match Schedule
• Team A vs Team B
• Team B vs Team C
• Team C vs Team A
Match Duration
• Each match shall consist of two halves of 7.5 minutes each.
• A 2-minute halftime break shall be provided.
• The team with the higher score at the end of the match shall be declared the winner.
• Each team is allowed one 1-minute Timeout per game (i.e., 2 timeouts total per game, one for each
team).
5. Qualification for the Final
• If one team loses both league matches, the remaining two teams shall qualify for the Final.
• If all three teams record one win each, the team with the higher points difference shall qualify.
• In case each team wins one game, qualification will be determined by Net Points (Points Scored
minus Points Conceded).
• If teams remain tied, the team with the higher total score shall qualify.
• If teams are still tied, a Tie-Breaker Raid shall be conducted.
• The Tie-Breaker Raid shall consist of 3 raids per team. If the scores remain tied after this, a
sudden-death 1 raid per team showdown shall be conducted to determine the winner.
6. Final Match
• The two qualified teams shall compete in the Final.
• The Final shall consist of two halves of 7.5 minutes each with a 2-minute halftime break.
• The team with the higher score at the end of the match shall be declared the Champion.
7. Referees & Officials
• All matches shall be conducted under the supervision of appointed referees and officials.
• Any disputes arising during the tournament shall be resolved by the referees and officials.
• The decision of the referees and officials shall be final and binding on all participants.
8. Awards
• Winners: 300 Team Points
• Runners-Up: 150 Team Points
• Gifts and Certificates will be distributed on the same day.
Reference Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=d-9eTjuXymY – The video is provided as a
reference guide to help participants understand the game and its basic rules. Please kindly refer to the
rules above.
A more detailed explanation of the rules, match procedures, scoring system, and referee interpretations
will be provided by the referees before the commencement of the tournament

name: Lemon & Spoon Race
weather_note: Quick fun race format with heats and finals.
rules_text:
General Team Registration
Each team may register up to 2 substitute participants for the event.
Substitutes may be utilized across the Male, Female, and Relay Categories before the commencement of the respective event.
Once a participant has begun competing in a category, substitutions shall not be permitted except with referee approval in case of injury.

MALE CATEGORY
1. Team Composition
Each team may nominate 2 male participants.
A total of 6 participants shall compete in this category (2 participants from each of the 3 teams).
2. Match Format
All participants shall compete individually.
The objective is to complete the designated course in the shortest possible time while balancing the lemon on the spoon.
Timing shall begin when the referee signals the start.
Timing shall end when the participant crosses the finish line.
3. Tournament Format
The preliminary stage shall consist of 2 sets.
Each set shall have 3 participants, with 1 participant from each team competing simultaneously.
At the end of both sets, the 3 fastest valid participants shall qualify for the Final.
4. Final Match & Tie-Breaker Rules
The 3 qualified participants shall compete simultaneously in the Final.
The participant recording the fastest valid time in the Final shall be declared the Winner.
The participant recording the second-fastest valid time in the Final shall be declared the Runner-Up.
If two or more participants are tied for qualification to the Final, a Tie-Breaker Race shall be conducted.
If the Final results in a tie, a Tie-Breaker Race shall be conducted immediately.
The participant recording the faster valid time in the tie-breaker shall be ranked higher.
5. Penalties & Disqualifications
Penalty Offences
If the lemon falls from the spoon at any point during the race, the participant must immediately return to the original starting line and restart the race from the beginning.
The timer shall continue running during the restart.
There is no limit on the number of restarts.
Disqualification Offences
Deliberately holding, securing, or balancing the lemon with any part of the body other than the spoon.
Deliberately obstructing or interfering with another participant.
Leaving the designated lane.
Starting before the referee's signal.
Receiving physical assistance from another person.
Unsportsmanlike conduct as determined by the referee.
6. Referees & Officials
The event shall be conducted under the supervision of appointed referees and officials.
Any dispute arising during the event shall be resolved by the referees and officials.
The decision of the referees and event officials shall be final and binding on all participants.
